about.title: CrossFit Coach
about.bio: I coach functional fitness — the kind that makes you stronger, faster, and more capable in and out of the gym. Whether you're brand new to CrossFit or an experienced athlete chasing competition, I meet you where you are and push you to where you want to be.

hero.headline: Move Well. Lift Heavy. Go Fast.
hero.subline: CrossFit coaching — foundations training, performance programming, and competition prep for athletes who want to earn their fitness.

packages.title: Foundations Program
packages.description: 8-session on-ramp program for new CrossFit athletes — movement standards, barbell technique, scaling options, and box culture. Required before joining group classes.

packages.title: Performance Training
packages.description: Ongoing group programming — 5 classes per week, structured periodization, strength bias, and a community that pushes you harder than you'd push yourself.

packages.title: Competition Prep
packages.description: Private coaching for athletes targeting the CrossFit Open, local throwdowns, or Sanctional qualifying — 3 extra sessions per week of gymnastics, barbell cycling, and strategy.

testimonials.quote: I walked in not being able to do a pull-up. Eight months later I got my first muscle-up. The coaching here is patient and the community keeps you coming back.

faq.question: Do I need to be fit to start CrossFit?
faq.answer: No — CrossFit is designed to scale to any fitness level. The Foundations program exists specifically to prepare you. You don't need to be fit to start — you start to get fit.

faq.question: What's included in the Foundations program?
faq.answer: 8 sessions covering fundamental movements — squats, deadlifts, press, clean, gymnastics basics, and how to read and pace a WOD. Foundationsgraduates have everything they need for group classes.

faq.question: How long are sessions?
faq.answer: Group classes are 60 minutes. Competition prep sessions are 75–90 minutes.

faq.question: What should I bring?
faq.answer: Athletic shoes (cross-trainers or lifting shoes for barbell work), athletic clothing, and water. Chalk and lifting belt provided.

faq.question: Do you train older athletes?
faq.answer: Yes — Masters athletes (40+) are welcome. Programming modifications account for recovery needs and movement restrictions.
